- **surface.notation-observer-frame** [notation] — Local-frame versus observer-frame quantities and compactness. Symbols relating local-frame surface quantities to those seen by a distant observer.  
  src: `potekhin_ho_chabrier_2016_review` Sect. 2.1, p. 4; Sect. 2.3, p. 8; anchor: “Stefan-Boltzmann law Lph”
- **surface.notation-temperatures** [notation] — Temperature symbols for the surface thermal map. Local, polar, equatorial, boundary, effective and redshifted temperatures used in the surface-temperature literature.  
  src: `potekhin_pons_page_2015_thermal` eqs. 39, 40; Sect. 5.1 (L1942-1943); App. B (L2674); anchor: “introduce the overall effective temperature of the”
- **surface.phc16-nonuniform-modulation** [result] — Non-uniform surface temperature and rotational modulation (PHC16). Since thermal diffusion is anisotropic in a strong magnetic field, the temperature is non-uniform over the stellar surface, which can lead to modulation of the observed thermal flux as the star rotates.  
  src: `potekhin_ho_chabrier_2016_review` Sect. 2.3, p. 8; anchor: “Since thermal diffusion is anisotropic in a strong magnetic field, the temperatu”
- **surface.phc16-redshift-relations** [equation] — Gravitational redshift relations for thermal emission (PHC16). With 1 + z_g = (1 - x_g)^{-1/2}, a thermal spectrum of effective temperature T_eff appears to a remote observer with T_eff^inf = T_eff/(1+z_g); the apparent radius is R^inf = R(1+z_g); the apparent luminosity is L^inf = L/(1+z_g)^2 = 4 pi sigma_SB (R^inf)^2 (T_eff^inf)^4 with local L = 4 pi sigma_SB R^2 T_eff^4.  
  `1+z_g=(1-x_g)^{-1/2},\quad T_{\rm eff}^\infty=T_{\rm eff}/(1+z_g),\quad R_\infty=R(1+z_g),\quad L^\infty_{\rm ph}=L_{\rm ph}/(1+z_g)^2=4\pi\sigma_{\rm SB}(R_\infty)^2(T_{\rm eff}^\infty)^4`  
  src: `potekhin_ho_chabrier_2016_review` Sect. 2.3, p. 8 (1+z_g definition: p. 4); anchor: “Stefan-Boltzmann law Lph”
- **surface.phc16-rxj1856-polar-field** [datum] — RX J1856.5-3754 piecewise-dipole fit: polar field. The thin magnetised-hydrogen-atmosphere-on-condensed-iron fit of RX J1856.5-3754 used a piecewise approximation to dipole-like distributions of magnetic field and temperature with polar field B_p of about 6e12 G.  
  src: `potekhin_ho_chabrier_2016_review` Sect. 5.1, p. 16; anchor: “with the polar values Bp ∼ 6 × 1012 G, Ts ∼ 0.7 MK, whereas the overall effectiv”
- **surface.phc16-rxj1856-polar-ts** [datum] — RX J1856.5-3754 piecewise-dipole fit: polar surface temperature. The RX J1856 thin magnetised hydrogen atmosphere over condensed iron fit reviewed from ref. [101] has polar local T_s ~ 0.7 MK.  
  src: `potekhin_ho_chabrier_2016_review` Sect. 5.1, p. 16; anchor: “with the polar values Bp ∼ 6 × 1012 G, Ts ∼ 0.7 MK, whereas the overall effectiv”
- **surface.phc16-rxj1856-teff-inf** [datum] — RX J1856.5-3754 overall redshifted effective temperature. The overall (redshifted) effective temperature in the RX J1856 thin hydrogen atmosphere over condensed iron fit reviewed from ref. [101] is T_eff^inf = 0.434 +/- 0.003 MK (1 sigma).  
  src: `potekhin_ho_chabrier_2016_review` Sect. 5.1, p. 16; anchor: “= 0.434 ± 0.003 MK (1σ significance)”
- **surface.phc16-ts-definition** [definition] — Local effective surface temperature T_s (PHC16). A local effective surface temperature T_s is defined by F_ph(theta, phi) = sigma_SB T_s^4, where F_ph is the local radial flux density at the surface point of polar angle theta and azimuth phi. Since L_ph is the integral of F_ph over the surface, T_eff^4 equals the surface average of T_s^4.  
  `F_{\rm ph}(\theta,\varphi) = \sigma_{\rm SB} T_{\rm s}^4`  
  src: `potekhin_ho_chabrier_2016_review` Sect. 2.3, p. 8; anchor: “relation Fph (θ , ϕ ) = σSB Ts4 , where Fph is the local radial flux density at ”
- **surface.ppp15-anisotropic-conduction-nonuniform** [result] — Non-uniform T_s from anisotropic conduction in strong fields. In strongly quantising fields heat conduction in the envelope is strongly anisotropic, so the effective local surface temperature T_s is non-uniform and depends on the magnetic-field geometry.  
  src: `potekhin_pons_page_2015_thermal` Sect. 5.2, p. 40; anchor: “Therefore the effective local surface temperature Ts is non-uniform and de-”
- **surface.ppp15-approx-1d-envelope** [approximation] — One-dimensional (radial) heat-blanketing approximation. Envelope thermal structure is computed in the 1D plane-parallel approximation with Fb = sigma_SB Ts^4 locally in the absence of neutrino energy losses in the envelope. It overestimates the heat-blanketing effect where the magnetic field is nearly tangential because heat then flows along field lines from hotter surface regions; for a dipole this is an equatorial band of width ~10 percent of the radius, which is also the coldest region, so its contribution to the total flux is negligible and the 1D approach reproduces the integrated observed flux. For magnetars with complex field geometry the 1D approach is not adequate and a 2D/3D treatment is required.  
  src: `potekhin_pons_page_2015_thermal` Sect. 5.1; Sect. 5.3, pp. 38, 41-42; anchor: “1D approximation overestimates the heat blanketing effect in regions with nearly”
- **surface.ppp15-approx-fit-validity** [approximation] — Domain of the PPP15 Appendix-B Tb-Ts fit. The fit B.1-B.6 was built on 2D magnetothermal data for non-accreted envelopes with a dipole field: rho_b = 1e10 g cm^-3, BSk21 EoS, 5 values of T_b (1e7-1e9 K), 5 values of B_p (1e11-1e15 G), 20 colatitudes 0..pi/2, supplemented by 1D polar calculations (36 T_b from 10^6.5 to 1e10 K, 9 B_p from 1e11 to 1e15 G). It includes crustal neutrino emission and supersedes Potekhin et al. (2003) for B > 1e12 G or T_b >~ 1e8 K. T_s is multiplied by a correction factor for electron-electron collisions obtained at B = 0.  
  src: `potekhin_pons_page_2015_thermal` App. B, pp. 51-52; anchor: “We stress that its use is restricted by non-accreted (i.e., composed of heavy”
- **surface.ppp15-fit-b1-polar-temperature** [equation] — Polar surface temperature fit without neutrino losses (PPP15 eqs. B.1-B.2). Effective surface temperature at the magnetic pole, neglecting crustal neutrino emission, as a function of envelope-bottom temperature T_b (via T_9), surface gravity g_14 and polar field B_12, for non-accreted envelopes.  
  `T_{\rm p}^{(0)} = \left[g_{14}\left(T_1^4 + (1+0.15\sqrt{B_{12}})\,T_0^4\right)\right]^{1/4}\times10^6\ {\rm K};\ \ T_0=(15.7\,T_9^{3/2}+1.36\,T_9)^{0.3796},\ \ T_1 = 1.13\,B_{12}^{0.119}T_9^{a},\ \ a=0.337/(1+0.02\sqrt{B_{12}})`  
  src: `potekhin_pons_page_2015_thermal` eqs. B.1-B.2, p. 52; anchor: “is approximately given by the expression”
- **surface.ppp15-fit-b3-neutrino-limit** [equation] — Neutrino-limited polar temperature and corrected pole temperature (PPP15 eqs. B.3-B.4). Limiting polar surface temperature at which T_p(T_b) levels off due to neutrino emission from the crust (B.3), and the corrected polar temperature that takes this limit into account (B.4).  
  `T_{\rm p}^{(\max)} = \left(5.2\,g_{14}^{0.65} + 0.093\sqrt{g_{14}B_{12}}\right)\times10^6\ {\rm K};\qquad T_{\rm p} = T_{\rm p}^{(0)}\left[1+\left(T_{\rm p}^{(0)}/T_{\rm p}^{(\max)}\right)^4\right]^{-1/4}`  
  src: `potekhin_pons_page_2015_thermal` eqs. B.3-B.4, p. 52; anchor: “The corrected surface temperature at the pole, which takes this limit into accou”
- **surface.ppp15-fit-b5-pole-equator-ratio** [equation] — Polar-to-equatorial surface temperature ratio fit (PPP15 eq. B.5). Rough fit for the ratio of the polar to the equatorial surface temperature as a function of T_9 and B_12. The ratio's numerically calculated dependence oscillates at B > 1e13 G; the fit converges to an average value there, with data deviations up to 35 percent, and typical errors of a few percent (up to 10 percent) for B <~ 3e12 G.  
  `\frac{T_{\rm p}}{T_{\rm eq}} = 1 + \frac{(1230\,T_9)^{3.35}B_{12}\sqrt{1+2B_{12}^2}}{(B_{12}+450\,T_9+119\,B_{12}T_9)^4} + \frac{0.0066\,B_{12}^{5/2}}{T_9^{1/2}+0.00258\,B_{12}^{5/2}}`  
  src: `potekhin_pons_page_2015_thermal` eq. B.5, p. 52; anchor: “The ratio of the polar to equatorial surface temperatures can be roughly evaluat”
- **surface.ppp15-fit-b6-colatitude-profile** [equation] — Surface temperature versus magnetic colatitude (PPP15 eq. B.6). Approximate dependence of the local surface temperature T_s on magnetic colatitude theta, interpolating between the polar temperature T_p (theta = 0) and the equatorial temperature T_eq (theta = pi/2), with coefficients a_1 and a_2 depending on T_9 and B_12.  
  `\frac{T_{\rm s}(\theta)-T_{\rm eq}}{T_{\rm p}-T_{\rm eq}} = \frac{(1+a_1+a_2)\cos^2\theta}{1+a_1\cos\theta+a_2\cos^2\theta},\quad a_1=\frac{a_2T_9^{1/2}}{3},\quad a_2=\frac{10B_{12}}{T_9^{1/2}+0.1B_{12}T_9^{-1/4}}`  
  src: `potekhin_pons_page_2015_thermal` eq. B.6, p. 52; anchor: “3. Finally, the dependence of the surface temperature on the magnetic colatitude”
- **surface.ppp15-fit-flux-recipe** [equation] — Flux through the envelope bottom with neutrino losses (PPP15 App. B item 4). In the absence of crustal neutrino emission and in the plane-parallel approximation the boundary flux is F_b = sigma_SB T_s^4; if a significant part of the energy is carried away by neutrinos, evaluate F_b = sigma_SB T_*^4 with T_* given by the above Ts approximations without the correction (B.4).  
  `F_{\rm b} = \sigma_{\rm SB}T_{\rm s}^4\ (Q_\nu\simeq0);\qquad F_{\rm b} = \sigma_{\rm SB}T_*^4\ (\text{with neutrino losses})`  
  src: `potekhin_pons_page_2015_thermal` App. B item 4, p. 52; anchor: “the flux through the boundary by the relation”
- **surface.ppp15-fit-structure** [definition] — Three-stage structure of the PPP15 temperature-map fit. The fit consists of three stages: (1) surface temperature at the magnetic pole T_p as a function of T_b, g and B_p; (2) the ratio of polar to equatorial surface temperature T_p/T_eq; (3) the dependence of T_s on magnetic colatitude theta. The local T_s map T_s(theta) is thus fixed by (T_b, g, B_p) through T_p, T_eq and the profile B.6.

For a dipole field in the Schwarzschild metric (Ginzburg and Ozernoy), the field strength at the stellar surface at magnetic polar angle chi is B(chi) = B_p sqrt(cos^2 chi + a^2 sin^2 chi), where B_p is the field strength at the magnetic pole, chi is the polar angle, and a = a(x) with x = r_g/R is given by surface.py01-gr-dipole-a-of-x. Ho et al. 2007 give R^infty for the B = 4e12 G atmosphere fit as 17 km (d_140 = 1) and state that the radius is given assuming d = 140 pc; the fit is linear in distance (the apparent radius fixes the normalisation (R^infty/d)^2 at fixed T^infty, z_g, N_H). At the Walter+2010 distance d = 123 pc: R^infty(123 pc) = R^infty(140 pc) x 123/140 = 17 km x 123/140 = 14.94 km (14.935714... km). This is a fixed-model rescaling (fixed atmospheric gravity, T^infty, N_H; Ho Sec. 6 prints R^infty ~ 17 (d/140 pc) km), not a self-consistent refit at 123 pc. NOTATION: Ho's R^infty is written R_{em}^\infty here to avoid colliding with the whole-star R^infty; d is written D. The T^infty = 4.34e5 K, z_g = 0.22 and N_H labels are not rescaled.
